review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the simp status of the lemmas it uses. In Mathlib, `map_j`, `variableChange_j` and `map_baseChange` are @[simp]. In TauCeti, `map_freyCurve`, `map_deuringNormalForm`, `freyCurve_j`, `deuringNormalForm_j` and `hasGoodReduction_minimal_smul_iff` are @[simp]. The only @[simp] declaration in the target, `hasPotentialGoodReduction_smul`, has a variable-change-free right side, so it terminates and does not compete with other rules. I found no loops or competing rules. I saw one gap: nothing rewrites `(W.baseChange L).j`, which is why two proofs spell the `j`-invariant transport out by hand. `WeierstrassCurve.baseChange` is a plain `def`, so the simp lemma `map_j` cannot fire on it. I searched TauCeti and Mathlib for a `WeierstrassCurve` lemma `baseChange_j` or `j_baseChange` and found none. The only `j_baseChange` hit is for `EllipticCurveGeom`, a different structure. I did not search outside the three readable roots. I could not run Lean, so the replacement below is untested.

findings.problem: The `j`-invariant of a base-changed curve has no canonical simp lemma. `WeierstrassCurve.baseChange` is a plain `def`, so the @[simp] lemma `map_j` does not fire on `(W.baseChange L).j` unless `baseChange` is unfolded by hand. The file therefore proves the same local fact twice, once as `hj` for `L` and once as `hjE` for `L'`. Each copy needs a `subst`, `rw [variableChange_j]` and `exact map_j W (algebraMap K L)`. The statements quantify over an auxiliary `W'` and an equation `C • W.baseChange L = W'` only to get around the missing rewrite. Later steps such as `rw [hjE _ hE, ...]` also depend on this indirection.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma to the elliptic-curve API: `@[simp] theorem baseChange_j (W : WeierstrassCurve K) [W.IsElliptic] (L) [Field L] [Algebra K L] : (W.baseChange L).j = algebraMap K L W.j`, proved by `map_j`. The `IsElliptic` instance for `W.baseChange L` must be found by instance search. If it is not found, state the lemma with `[(W.baseChange L).IsElliptic]` as `deuringNormalForm_j` does. Then `variableChange_j` and this lemma together give `(C • W.baseChange L).j = algebraMap K L W.j` by `simp`. Both `hj` and `hjE` collapse to one line, for example `by simp` after `subst`, or the `W'` parameter can be dropped.
findings.benefit: Readers get one canonical normal form for `j` of a base change, `algebraMap K L W.j`, instead of two copies of the same four-line argument. Other proofs that rewrite `j` through `baseChange` can also use `simp` instead of unfolding `baseChange` first.

evidence.excerpt: def baseChange [Algebra R A] : WeierstrassCurve A :=

rw [variableChange_j]
    exact map_j W (algebraMap K L')
